exposure: maternal ethnicity (Turkish vs. Syrian immigrant/refugee women)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, cesarean-section rates, hospitalization, SGA/LGA birth rates)
cohort: The study included 323 mother-infant pairs, consisting of Turkish and Syrian immigrant/refugee women, from Buca Seyfi Demirsoy Hospital in Izmir, Turkey.
finding: Pre-pregnancy BMI and gestational weight gain significantly affected some neonatal outcomes, with overweight/obese mothers having higher birth weights and cesarean-section rates.
mod_finding: Overweight/obese mothers had higher cesarean-section rates.
